title: Aviation Safety Case Method Applied to AI: Writing a Structured Safety Argument for an LLM Deployment

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: demonstrating the gap between aviation-grade governance and AI practice is informative, but a single prototype safety case has limited direct impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: Goal Structuring Notation is a specialized methodology from safety engineering; learning and applying it correctly requires domain expertise beyond beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: one specific deployment scenario, one safety case document. The scope is naturally bounded by the single-case approach.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is directly addressed by substantial recent work. 'A Structured Approach to Safety Case Construction for AI Systems' (arXiv:2601.22773, Jan 2026) conducted a systematic literature review and provides reusable templates for AI safety cases using GSN and CAE notations. 'Safety Cases: How to Justify the Safety of Advanced AI Systems' (arXiv:2403.10462, Anthropic et al., 2024) lays out the full methodology. The UK AISI has an active safety cases program. 'The BIG Argument for AI Safety Cases' (arXiv:2503.11705, 2025) extends the framework. GovAI published a cyber inability safety case template. CoDefeater (arXiv:2407.13717) uses LLMs to find defeaters in assurance cases. The FAA published a 'Roadmap for AI Safety Assurance' addressing aviation-specific GSN for AI. The core contribution — writing a structured safety argument for an LLM deployment using aviation safety case methodology — is thoroughly covered.
